'''Double Braced''' is an [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effect]] for several ship modules and weapons. It adds hardened supports that increase the receiving module's integrity without changing its mass or power draw.

== Effect ==

For most compatible modules, Double Braced provides:

* '''Module integrity:''' +15%
* '''Mass:''' no change
* '''Power draw:''' no change

The [[Frame Shift Drive]] version provides a larger '''+25% integrity''' modifier. The effect improves the module's own damage tolerance; it does not add hull strength or resistance to the ship as a whole.<ref name="inara-effects">[https://inara.cz/elite/experimentaleffects/ INARA: Experimental effects], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref><ref name="fandom-double">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Double_Braced Elite Dangerous Wiki: Double Braced], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref>

== Compatible modules ==

Double Braced is available for:

* [[Frame Shift Drive|Frame Shift Drives]], [[Power Plant|Power Plants]], [[Thrusters]], [[Shield Generator|Shield Generators]], and [[Shield Booster|Shield Boosters]];
* [[Beam Laser|Beam Lasers]], [[Burst Laser|Burst Lasers]], [[Pulse Laser|Pulse Lasers]], multi-cannons, [[Plasma Accelerator|Plasma Accelerators]], [[Fragment Cannon|Fragment Cannons]], [[Cannon|Cannons]], and [[Railgun|Rail Guns]];
* [[Mine Launcher|Mine Launchers]], [[Torpedo Pylon|Torpedo Pylons]], [[Seeker Missile Rack|Seeker Missiles]], and dumbfire missiles.

The effect can be installed by an [[Engineers|Engineer]] whose workshop supports Engineering for the receiving module type. Experimental Effects must be installed at an Engineer workshop and cannot be pinned for [[Remote Engineering]].

== Materials ==

Applying Double Braced requires:

* 3 Tungsten
* 5 Vanadium
* 1 Compound Shielding

These materials are consumed once when the effect is applied. Replacing Double Braced with another Experimental Effect consumes the new effect's materials.

== When to use it ==

Double Braced is most useful when keeping a particular module operational matters more than reducing mass or improving another performance characteristic. It can reinforce an FSD on a combat ship, strengthen an exposed power plant, or add damage tolerance to weapons and defensive modules without changing the ship's power budget.

It competes directly with effects that improve module performance. An exploration build may prefer [[Stripped Down]] on a heavy compatible module, while an FSD focused on jump range will usually favour [[Mass Manager]]. Choose Double Braced when extra module integrity solves a specific survivability problem rather than as a default addition to every build.
